title: AVX-512 / AVX2 Accelerated 32-Qubit Quantum State-Vector Simulator with Gate Fusion
objective: Implement an ultra-fast, multi-threaded 32-qubit state-vector quantum circuit simulator in C++20 accelerated by hand-optimized AVX2 / AVX-512 complex arithmetic intrinsics. The engine must support arbitrary quantum gates (Hadamard, Pauli-X/Y/Z, Phase/T gates, parameterized Rotation gates Rx, Ry, Rz, and two-qubit entangling gates CNOT, CZ, SWAP), static unitary gate fusion (merging sequences of single-qubit and two-qubit gates into dense 4x4 or 8x8 unitary matrix kernels), cache-blocking state-vector strides, and parallel multi-qubit measurement sampling.
motivation: Quantum circuit simulation is heavily compute- and memory-bandwidth-bound (2^32 complex amplitudes require 64 GB of memory in complex64). Pushing simulation performance requires advanced SIMD complex multiplication, cache-locality optimization across non-contiguous index strides, and algebraic gate fusion.
difficultyExplanation:
1. SIMD Complex Arithmetic on Strided Amplitudes: Applying quantum gates across non-contiguous qubit target indices requires fast SIMD permutations (_mm256_permute2f128_ps, _mm256_shuffle_ps) to avoid strided memory access bottlenecks.
2. Algebraic Gate Fusion: Analyzing circuit DAGs to automatically coalesce consecutive 1-qubit and 2-qubit operations acting on overlapping target qubits into fused multi-qubit unitary matrices to minimize memory bandwidth passes.
3. Multi-Threaded Cache-Blocking: Partitioning the 2^N state vector into L1/L2 cache-sized sub-blocks so multiple gates can be applied in SRAM without round-tripping to main RAM.
environmentSummary: Ubuntu 24.04 with gcc-13, clang-18, cmake, ninja-build, and Python 3.12 verification harness in /app. Starter repository includes complex arithmetic vector abstractions, basic quantum gate definitions, state vector memory allocators, and unit test runners.
oracleStrategy: Reference C++20 implementation providing AVX2/AVX-512 fused 2x2 and 4x4 unitary kernels, OpenMP thread partitioning, and an automated circuit DAG fusion optimizer.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes four verification channels:
1. Basic Gate Superposition & Entanglement Verification (Bell state, GHZ state, QFT-8).
2. Quantum Random Circuit Sampling (RCS) Fidelity Test on 24-30 qubits (asserting state vector fidelity F >= 0.999999 against exact mathematical tensor contraction).
3. Static Unitary Gate Fusion Correctness (verifying fused matrix operators produce exact mathematical outputs across random rotation angles).
4. SIMD Performance & Throughput Benchmark (verifying >= 8x speedup over un-fused baseline and 0 ASan errors).
binarySuccessCondition: State vector fidelity F >= 0.99999 across all test circuits, zero race conditions, and >= 8x execution speedup over baseline un-fused simulator.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 25%: Basic single-qubit and two-qubit gate simulation correctness.
- 25%: Multi-qubit entanglement & QFT state fidelity.
- 25%: Static gate fusion DAG optimization.
- 25%: AVX2 SIMD acceleration throughput speedup (>= 8x).
anticipatedExploits:
1. Hardcoding final state vectors: Verifier generates dynamic random quantum circuits with random continuous angles (theta, phi, lambda) at evaluation time.
2. Dropping low-probability amplitudes: Verifier checks state normalization (sum of squared amplitudes == 1.0) and fidelity against exact double-precision math.
